title: Lineage I foundational body plan
scope: Foundational body plan of Lineage I, the six-limbed filament-and-scute lineage, including the wing-pair derivation used by its winged branches; usable within shared-setting ecology and adopted downstream story development.
claims: Lineage I descends from a six-limbed ancestor with a tail.
Branches repurpose limb pairs for locomotion, handling, display, defence, digging, climbing, swimming, or flight.
The outer covering combines insulating or sensory filaments with flexible scutes, in proportions varying by branch and body region.
Reproduction uses flexible, mineral-latticed brood eggs that require guarded nests or brooding.
Large-bodied branches reproduce slowly, making breeding adults and successful nesting sites ecologically consequential.
In winged branches the middle limb pair becomes the wing pair, leaving four well-spaced walking legs with wings rising near the body's centre of mass.
In non-flying branches the middle pair carries the lineage's most variable roles, including grasping, digging, display, and reduced vestiges.
Winged branches build flight surfaces from the lineage's existing filament-and-scute materials rather than novel membranes.
boundaries: Filament, scute, brood egg, and wing pair are author-facing functional descriptions, not in-world names or formal taxonomy.
The covering establishes no fur, feather, hair, reptile-scale, or turtle-scute homology; the six-limbed frame establishes no insect, vertebrate, or Earth-tetrapod homology.
Species, names, sizes, proportions, colours, lifespans, and the branch inventory remain open.

Warm-active describes sustained activity and thermal independence at qualitative grain; exact thermoregulation, metabolic rates, temperature tolerances, torpor, hibernation, and seasonal strategies remain open.
Limb repurposing lists possible roles, not a fixed branch map; no particular branch, limb configuration, or role combination is established.

Wing structure, vane or brace arrangement, wingspan, size ceilings, flight performance, launch, endurance, range, gliding branches, and flightless descendants of flyers remain open; mid-pair derivation establishes wing position and leg count only, not aerodynamic capability.

Brood eggs are flexible and mineral-latticed at qualitative grain; exact lattice chemistry, shell mechanics, size, clutch size, incubation period, temperature needs, hatching, and viability remain open.

Guarded nests or brooding establish a care requirement, not a guarantee of success, a fixed nest form, site type, parental sex or number, colony behaviour, or defence capability; nests can fail, and no branch is established as live-bearing.
Slow large-body reproduction is a qualitative tendency; no reproductive rate, age at maturity, population size, or recovery time is established.
Lineage II's live birth from retained egg capsules belongs to a separate lineage and is unaffected by this record.

No Lineage I branch is established as present, abundant, or absent at any particular location, including the initial basin, and no branch is identified with any megafaunal, mythic, returning, or settlement-adjacent animal.
Diet, digestion, senses, cognition, sociality, communication, migration, disease, and predator-prey relationships remain open.

Mana patterns remain open; no Mana organ, specialised ability, System progression, universal creature level, spawn mechanism, reward, Skill, trait payload, or Ancestry Development rule is established.
Earth life of any era and mythological creatures may inspire author-facing design; no living, extinct, or legendary Earth species is transplanted directly.
Food, energy, materials, reproduction, disease, injury, mortality, and carrying capacity remain binding ecological constraints.
story_implications: The lineage can supply both ordinary six-limbed animals and four-legs-plus-wings silhouettes.
Guarded nest sites become defensible, losable, story-bearing places.
Slow-breeding large branches make sustained hunting or habitat pressure consequential rather than instantly recoverable.
Every species, branch, local presence, and encounter requires its own evidence and records.
system_implications: The body plan describes ordinary planetary ecology under CAL0 WLD1.2D and WLD2.1A+D.
No System mechanic, creature progression rule, spawn source, reward, or specialised Mana ability is established.
research_questions: What branches exist, and how do their limb configurations and sizes vary?
What wing structures do filament-and-scute flight surfaces produce, and what size ceilings follow?
What filament and scute microstructure, moult, colour, and sensory functions occur?
What egg-lattice chemistry, clutch sizes, incubation, and parental roles apply?
Which branches, if any, occur in the initial basin and wider region?
What Mana patterns, if any, characterise the lineage?

author_approval.evidence: After the A/B/C wing-derivation cards were presented with A recommended, the Author selected 'A — Middle pair' on 2026-08-17.
